highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially launched Claude Opus 5, the most powerful model in the Claude lineup, featuring a 1M token context window and a fast mode priced at $10/$50 per million tokens. This is now the default Opus model in Claude Code, meaning your existing workflows automatically benefit from the upgrade. Developers working on large codebases will especially appreciate the expanded context window for handling entire projects in a single session.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.222: Worktree Isolation Security Fix
highlights.summary: This release patches two important security issues: worktree-isolated sessions and their subagents can no longer run destructive git commands against your main checkout, and PreToolUse auto-allow hooks can no longer bypass tool restrictions in background agent tasks. If you use git worktrees or background agents in your workflow, updating immediately is strongly recommended to protect your main branch from accidental or unintended destructive operations.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.221: Focus View for VS Code
highlights.summary: The VS Code extension now includes a Focus View mode that hides noisy tool activity logs behind a clean, expandable per-turn summary with a live running-tool indicator. You can toggle it instantly with Ctrl+Alt+F or via the command palette using 'Claude Code: Toggle Focus view'. This is a great quality-of-life improvement if you find the tool activity stream distracting while Claude is working on longer tasks.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219: Opus 5 Default + Strict Network Sandbox
highlights.summary: Beyond adding Claude Opus 5 as the default Opus model, this release introduces a `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` setting that blocks all non-allowlisted hosts for sandboxed commands without prompting — giving you tighter control over what network resources your agent can reach. A new `DirectoryAdded` hook also fires after a directory is added, enabling more advanced automation workflows.

highlights.title: Claude Code Basics | Master 95% in 10 Minutes
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial promises to get you up to speed with the most essential Claude Code features in just 10 minutes, making it ideal if you're just getting started or want a fast refresher. It covers the core workflows that cover the vast majority of everyday use cases. Bookmark this as a go-to resource to share with teammates who are new to Claude Code.

highlights.title: How Does Claude Code Actually Work? Let's Make Our Own
highlights.summary: This deep-dive video breaks down the internal mechanics of Claude Code by walking through building a simplified version from scratch, giving you genuine insight into how the tool calls, context management, and agent loop actually function. Understanding the internals helps you write better prompts and debug unexpected behavior more effectively. Highly recommended if you've been using Claude Code for a while and want to level up your mental model.

highlights.title: Agent Skills That Bring Team Coding Standards to Claude Code and Codex
highlights.summary: This open-source project lets teams encode their coding standards, conventions, and best practices as reusable 'agent skills' that Claude Code and Codex can automatically apply during development. It's a practical solution for keeping AI-generated code consistent with your team's style guide without having to repeat instructions in every session. Worth exploring if you're rolling out Claude Code across an engineering team and want to enforce consistent output.

highlights.title: 9-Minute Beginner Guide: Claude Code Installation, How It Works, and Real Usage (China Direct Access)
highlights.summary: This Bilibili video offers a concise Chinese-language walkthrough of installing Claude Code, understanding how it works under the hood, and using it for real development tasks — with a focus on accessibility for users in mainland China. It's especially useful for Chinese-speaking developers who have struggled with connectivity or setup issues. The video aims to get you productive in under 10 minutes with no prior AI coding tool experience required.

tips_of_the_day: Use the new Focus View in VS Code (Ctrl+Alt+F) when you need to concentrate — it collapses Claude's tool activity into a single summary line so you can stay in flow while long tasks run in the background.

If your team keeps repeating the same coding style instructions at the start of every Claude Code session, consider writing a shared CLAUDE.md file at the repo root to encode those standards permanently — Claude Code loads it automatically on startup.

Before upgrading Claude Code in a project that uses git worktrees or background agents, read the v2.1.222 changelog carefully: the new isolation rules mean subagents can no longer touch your main checkout, which may change behavior you were previously relying on.
